subject: DPIA alignment + subprocessor sampling & transfer chain mapping
messages:
From: Maya R. Kumar <maya.kumar@greenstream.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Greenstream Security Team <security@greenstream.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: DPIA alignment + sampling plan for subprocessors

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. As we prepare our procurement package for the upcoming onboarding window, our legal and security teams asked for two specific deliverables we need by next week to close the vendor risk review:

1) A brief sampling plan for subprocessor evidence (how you choose sample sets, retention of artifacts, and expected turnaround for ad-hoc evidence pulls).
2) A transfer-chain mapping (Article 28/30-focused) that shows where customer data may transit between Redwood and subprocessors, and the contractual mechanisms in place (SCCs, onshore fallbacks, or equivalent).

We also need confirmation whether you can provide a DPIA excerpt demonstrating processing purpose alignment for our use case (NLP inference over customer-supplied text) and whether any subprocessors perform full-text indexing.

Can you share a short package and an estimate for how quickly you can deliver a minimal evidence bundle (logs + ledger excerpt + custody notes)?

Appreciate it — Maya

--
Maya Kumar
Security & Privacy Manager
Greenstream Corp
maya.kumar@greenstream.com
(415) 555-0127
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya R. Kumar <maya.kumar@greenstream.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: DPIA alignment + sampling plan for subprocessors

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can assemble the materials you listed. Quick clarifications so we scope correctly:

- By "sampling plan" do you prefer a deterministic sampling (e.g., quarterly stratified sampling across subprocessor categories) or event-driven (e.g., sample on each onboarding / major config change)?
- For the DPIA excerpt: we can provide the section that maps processing activities to safeguards and residual risk, but we do not publish full customer DPIAs — would an excerpt focused on inference and data flows suffice?
- Regarding full-text indexing: our search/indexing subprocessors do not index customer plaintext unless explicitly enabled via a product feature; default inference paths do not store full-text beyond short-term KV caches. We can document cache retention windows and encryption-in-transit/rest controls.

I'll loop in Irene (privacy) and Ben (sales / contract ops) to confirm the artifacts and turnaround. Targeting a draft bundle by EOD Friday PT.

Best,
Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager\Redwood Inference\sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: DPIA alignment + sampling plan for subprocessors

Sofia / Ben —

Draft plan below (internal). Happy to adjust before we send external:

- Sampling approach: hybrid model
  * Quarterly stratified sample: pick 3 subprocessors per criticality tier (high/medium/low) and pull artifacts for the most recent 30-day window.
  * Event-driven sample: for any major config change or new subprocessor onboarding in the quarter, include that subprocessor in the next ad-hoc pull.
- Artifacts to include in bundle: processing ledger excerpt (CSV), KMS wrap/CMK attestations (redacted where necessary), network egress summary (per-region), and a short chain-of-custody note for the requested time window.
- Turnaround: standard quarterly pulls within 7 business days; ad-hoc event-driven pulls targeted at 10 business days (can be expedited to 3 with approved SOW/fee).
- Article 28/30 mapping: we can provide a concise transfer-chain map (diagram + table) that lists subprocessor role, country, legal mechanism (SCCs / onshore fallback / Binding Corporate Rules), and whether they process tokens or store persistent PII.

Attachments to prepare for Greenstream:
  - subprocessor-sampling-plan.pdf (this will outline methodology and schedule)
  - processing-ledger-excerpt.csv (sample ledger rows for the selected timeframe)
  - art28-30-summary.pdf (transfer chain mapping + contractual mechanisms)

Ben — can you confirm any contractual considerations (SLA for evidence delivery, redaction standard) and whether Sales wants to offer the expedited evidence turnaround as part of the onboarding package?

Irene

--
Irene Choi
Director, Privacy Operations\Redwood Inference\irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Maya R. Kumar <maya.kumar@greenstream.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPIA alignment + sampling plan for subprocessors

Maya / Irene / Sofia —

Thanks — looping me in works. Greenstream, quick summary and next steps:

- We will deliver the minimal evidence bundle by Friday 2027-07-02 EOD PT as a temporary package to unblock procurement. That package will include the three attachments (sampling plan, ledger excerpt, Art 28/30 summary).
- Standard delivery SLA for ad-hoc evidence pulls is 10 business days; we can expedite to 3 business days with an expedited support addendum (commonly accepted for enterprise onboarding).
- Next steps:
  1) Sofia/Irene to upload the draft bundle to the shared Drive link and attach a short cover note.
  2) Greenstream to confirm whether they need redacted KMS key IDs (we typically provide key metadata without exposing raw key material).
  3) If they require formal DPIA documentation beyond the excerpt, Sales will route that request to Legal for an engagement plan.

Maya — hope this addresses the timeline. If you want the expedited lane, tell us and I will open an SOW addendum and route to Finance.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference\ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
